result:
The best-supported answer is α = 2, so Solution 2 has the correct final answer. I am relying partly on recall of a known result and did not derive the bound myself.

I recall a result of this form: every graph G has a tree decomposition of width at most about 2·tw(G)+1 in which each vertex v lies in O(d(v)+1) bags. I also recall that the factor 2 cannot be improved, so no c < 2 works. This matches Solution 2's answer of 2. I did not verify its freeing construction or its lower-bound argument in detail.

- **Solution 1** claims that any c > 1 works, justified only by an informal grid construction. That claim is implausible and unsupported. It contradicts the sharpness of the factor 2.
- **Solution 3** claims that P(c) fails for every finite c, using cycles. This is wrong because a cycle has a tree decomposition of width 2 with bounded spread (a fan or triangulation-style decomposition). Its "Ω(log n)" lower bound for cycles is unjustified. Treewidth-2 graphs with larger allowed width are handled by the known construction with c = 2.

CHOICE: 2
